acceptance: 1) Entry: admin Personal information (admin-account-link) -> /admin/account. Data source: GET /api/admin/account. login-mode-toggle sends POST reauth(LOGIN_MODE) before PATCH login-mode; actual totp sign-in with the next code then needs no password. Reject removing all methods, and display the old value after 409 (E-06, E-07, E-09). 2) change-password uses a PASSWORD grant with POST password. change-authenticator uses a TOTP_RESET grant with POST 2fa/reset, then the visible Continue setup control enters /admin-recovery. Each click asserts real purpose/target/body and persisted outcomes. An already-used code step prompts waiting for the next code; five-minute expiry or wrong-purpose grants do not submit (E-72, E-73, E-74). 3) A user who forgot the current password can still work through totp sign-in, but sensitive controls offer no session-only/TOTP-only substitute. Recovery uses only the independent restricted page. Clear password/TOTP when verification ends; grants remain memory-only and unknown responses do not replay (E-75). Use the unique minimalist-flat style from section 11. At the actual service at 1920x1080, 1440x900, and 390x844, record GIFs and computed styles: 2px black borders, zero radius, no shadow, and accent #b45700. On each admin page, run D1-D6 and overflow probes with work/form/card and density7/gutter16/gap16/pad16. Labels and keyboard focus are reachable; touch-control targets measure at least 44px. 4) Add only page-request/display assertions for this card, reusing passing T3/T16/T20 transaction cases. Entering /admin/account sends GET /api/admin/account with status 200; switch checked equals passwordlessEnabled. Clicking login-mode-toggle opens ReauthDialog with current-password/six-digit-totp fields. Submission sends POST /api/admin/account/reauth with purpose=LOGIN_MODE. Only after a 200 token/purpose/expiresAt response may PATCH /api/admin/account/login-mode send body={passwordlessEnabled,actionGrant:token}. Its 200 response returns the submitted Boolean and timestamp changedAt. The old session's next GET account returns 401 and /admin-login is displayed. After 409 the switch restores the old GET value and shows an error, not saved-success. change-password uses purpose=PASSWORD and POST /api/admin/account/password body containing newPassword/actionGrant; 200 with ok=true and reauthRequired=true returns to login. change-authenticator uses purpose=TOTP_RESET and POST /api/admin/account/2fa/reset with actionGrant; 200 with reenrollRequired=true/enrollLink shows Continue setup, whose click reaches pathname=/admin-recovery. Reauth failure 401 returns no token, shows a dialog error, and sends no subsequent sensitive write; a consumed time step prompts waiting for the next code. An expired/wrong-purpose grant makes the target write return 401/error=action_grant_invalid, leaves before/after settings GETs equal, and requests fresh verification. With a forgotten password, session-only or TOTP-only reauth returns 401 without token while original totp sign-in still works. The page does not send a passwordless reauth substitute or add recovery codes back to the ordinary form. Closing dialog/pagehide removes password/totp/grant from input values and browser persistent storage. After an unknown write response, observe 15 seconds without an automatic repeated POST/PATCH; only GET may verify current settings.

E-06.scene: C-03 Authenticator enrollment and the passwordless-default toggle
E-06.trigger: The owner of an enrolled account enables the toggle after fresh identity verification.
E-06.expect: Ordinary sign-in requires only an email address or account identifier and an authenticator code. Recovery codes belong to a separate recovery entry point; a password is no longer required for this mode.

E-07.scene: C-03 Authenticator enrollment and the passwordless-default toggle
E-07.trigger: Disabling passwordless mode or unbinding the authenticator would leave the account with no usable sign-in method.
E-07.expect: Reject the change. First finish setting up and verifying a usable password or alternative method, and then commit the switch atomically.

E-09.scene: C-03 Authenticator enrollment and the passwordless-default toggle
E-09.trigger: The interface retains the user's term 2FA.
E-09.expect: Explain that the current passwordless mode is Account + authenticator code. An account identifier is not an independent authentication factor; do not claim the security level of two independent factors.

E-72.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-72.trigger: The same TOTP time step has already been consumed by sign-in, another sensitive operation, or a concurrent request.
E-72.expect: Atomically consume the account's authenticator time step so later requests cannot issue another ActionGrant. The client may wait for the next code and retry; do not reintroduce recovery codes into ordinary sign-in.

E-73.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-73.trigger: Two requests use the same ActionGrant concurrently, or a password-change grant is used to disable the authenticator.
E-73.expect: Within the sensitive-change transaction, validate and consume the grant once against the action, device, account, and credential version. Only one matching request succeeds; reject a mismatched purpose without executing the change.

E-74.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-74.trigger: More than five minutes have elapsed since grant issuance, the device is revoked, the password/authenticator changes, or the account's permission becomes invalid.
E-74.expect: The old grant immediately becomes invalid. Fresh-verification grants cannot be transferred between devices and cannot extend the original device-session lifetime.

E-75.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-75.trigger: The user forgets the current password but can still use previously enabled passwordless sign-in.
E-75.expect: Resolve D3 through the restricted recovery path and one-time permit/restricted cookie already defined in sections 09/10. Ordinary passwordless sign-in remains unchanged. Without the current password, sensitive settings cannot issue an ordinary ActionGrant: reject direct requests based solely on a signed-in session or one TOTP without a change. Restricted recovery permits only new enrollment and is audited.
